newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks gain as golds shine.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks gain as golds shine.

text.p: Toronto stocks rallied to close higher on Friday, gaining almost 1.2 percent on the back of stronger golds.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index jumped 72.05 points to 6229.52. Trading totaled 117 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).

"The gold sector is coming back in vogue," said Pier Donnini, head trader of institutional equities at Yorkton Securities. Bullion prices on New York's COMEX rose $4.50 to $349.30, rebounding from recent lows, Donnini said.
Donnini added that bullion prices historically rallied in the spring. Toronto's gold group jumped 3.7 percent on Friday.
The broad-based rally included all of Toronto's 14 sub-indices and was led by golds, media, oils and banks.
Advancing issues almost doubled decliners 637 to 336, while 281 closed flat.
In the past week, Canada's largest equity market rose by 122 points or almost two percent.
The 300 Index is 118 points below its all-time high of 6348, set on March 11.
ScotiaMcLeod Director of Equities Trading Fred Ketchen said that level would be soon be breached.
"I don't think it will be too long before we reach that and hit new highs," he said.
Barrick Gold Corp., the sixth most heavily weighted issue on the 300 Index, rose 1.30 to 35.30. Placer Dome Inc. rose 0.80 to 26.40.
Ault Foods Ltd. rose 4 to 29.75, outstripping the share price in a takeover bid by privately held Saputo Group Inc. Saputo offered C$28 a share for the dairy foods producer.
